title: Airfloa Rail Technology Ltd - 544516 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 143% to INR220.3 crore and PAT rose 108% to INR25.1 crore, with an 11.4% PAT margin inside the 10-12% guidance band.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR220.3 crore (up 143% YoY), EBITDA of INR48.4 crore (up 120%, 21.9% margin) and PAT of INR25.1 crore (up 108%, 11.4% margin). The quarter included the completed acquisition of KIN Railway Equipment for INR41 crore plus GST, which brings an order book of about INR180 crore. Management said it is being disciplined on bids, re-tendering at revised prices after aluminium cost increases, and that H1 order inflow was only about INR49 crore. Aerospace and defence remain at an early stage, and management guided to FY27 revenue of INR500 crore-plus and FY28 revenue of INR750 crore.

financial_highlights.value: Broadly stable, management says at higher end
About INR140 crore (analyst figure; management referred to about INR150 crore)

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Management says the FY27 and FY28 numbers are more than 90% railway-based. Focus areas are Amrit Bharat, EMU, MEMU, Vande Bharat, metro and refurbishment, and the Vande Bharat sleeper interior-design contract is worth INR34.85 crore incl. GST.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence
segments.commentary: Management puts this at about 10% of FY27-28 revenue and expects a significant rise in FY28. Focus is on drones, anti-drones, autonomous systems, precision-guided ammunition, and ISRO satellite testing. Big Bang Boom JV is still pending and management said it will be announced in days or weeks.

segments.name: KIN Railway Equipment (acquired)
segments.commentary: Coimbatore facility of more than 2 lakh sq ft, with an order book of about INR180 crore. Management expects better margins from its metro business and says the facility is approved by Alstom, Hitachi and Siemens for exports.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR500 crore and above maintained.
FY28 revenue guidance of INR750 crore, with PAT margin of 10-12%.
Order book at 15 Nov 2026 of about INR610 crore incl. KIN; plan to execute INR280 crore in the balance of FY27.
Targeting fresh order inflows of INR450 crore over the coming months; expects an unexecuted order book of INR750-800 crore at end FY27.
Target EBITDA margin of 20-30%, with management saying it could be reached in 6 months to 1 year; it declined to commit to a 15-18% PAT margin for FY28.
Expects debtor days to fall within about 6 months and positive operating cash flow in FY28.
Says no equity raise is needed for at least 6-7 months; expects about INR100 crore more borrowing over two years.
capex_capacity: KIN acquisition completed for INR41 crore plus GST cash; Coimbatore facility of more than 2 lakh sq ft to be rebranded as the international business facility.
Investments made in Big Bang Boom defence projects, which management says are running ahead of plan.
Platform screen door business with KTK Group (MoU): market about INR2,000 crore a year, growing INR1,500-2,000 crore a year in India.
Management says it may raise equity only if large defence or aerospace orders convert into tangible orders.
demand_pricing: H1 order inflow was about INR49 crore per the analyst; management attributed the slow inflow to selective bidding for profitable orders.
Management said it could win INR1,000-2,000 crore orders on current conditions but is choosing only profitable ones.
Aluminium and other input price increases hit economics of some projects; re-tendering at revised prices has started.

Vande Bharat sleeper interior-design contract from ICF Chennai (with BLUE Engineering S.r.l.), INR34.85 crore incl. GST, completion within 12 months of LoA. Described as the first Indian engineering contract of its kind from Indian Railways.
Management says the KTK platform screen door MoU lets it bid as frontline partner for Delhi, Chennai and Bangalore metro tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 order inflow only INR49 crore, and where will the INR450 crore of H2 inflows come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slow inflow reflects selective bidding for profitable orders; the INR450 crore is expected mainly from railways and partly from defence and aerospace. It cited an order book of about INR610 crore as of 15 Nov 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin do new orders carry, and when can 30% be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets a 20-30% EBITDA margin (currently 22%), with the goal to be reached in 6 months to 1 year, and no fixed cap. The PAT baseline stays at 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Will receivables improve, and when does operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: About 78.2% of receivables are within 180 days and about 20% are beyond. Management said debtor days should fall within about 6 months and targets positive operating cash flow in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company need additional equity or peak borrowing for INR750 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current borrowings, including about INR100 crore for working capital, are enough for the INR750 crore plan for at least a year. Equity may be needed only if large defence orders materialise, and not within 6-7 months.

qa_highlights.question: Do FY28 revenue targets include aerospace and defence, and what is the split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY28 is more than 90% railways and about 10% aerospace and defence. The defence pipeline includes tender orders of INR50-150 crore and the Make-1 government programme, which needs about one year of development.

qa_highlights.question: Can PAT margin reach 15-18% in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to 15-18%, saying it aims to exceed 18% but will hold a 10-12% floor.

risks_watch: Receivables of about INR263 crore with 21.8% beyond 180 days; collection timing is critical to the cash-flow target.
The FY28 INR750-800 crore order book depends on INR450 crore of fresh inflows, against H1 inflows of about INR49 crore.
Defence and aerospace revenue depends on long qualification cycles and on the Big Bang Boom JV, which has been delayed and has no firm date.
Input cost volatility (aluminium) and re-tendering at revised prices may affect margin and order volume.
KIN integration and whether its metro business lifts margins as management expects.
Borrowings and interest cost (8.25-8.5%) rise with the planned working capital and expansion; the analyst figure of INR140 crore differs from management's INR150 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins but evasive on order timing, defence specifics and the JV, which management says cannot be disclosed yet. Answers on the PAT and EBITDA targets were hedged, with management saying it cannot commit to numbers beyond the 10-12% PAT band.
key_quotes: Our PAT margins remained within the guidance range of 10% to 12% that we have communicated to the investors.
I am not running behind the orders, I am running behind the profits.
Platform screen door business is approximately a INR2,000 crores business in a year.
But if you ask me, I would remain to be focusing on railway business in a bigger way.

adds.what: KIN Railway Equipment Coimbatore facility (>2 lakh sq ft), acquired and to be rebranded as international business facility

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR500 crore and above (held) and FY28 at INR750 crore; H1 FY27 revenue rose 143% and the INR610 crore order book (incl. KIN, ~INR180 crore) plus planned INR280 crore execution in the balance of FY27 partly backs it, but H1 order inflow was only ~INR49 crore against a target of INR450 crore, so the guidance is only partly covered by fresh orders.

oneOffs.what: KIN Railway Equipment acquired for INR41 crore plus GST, consolidated in H1 FY27 with an INR180 crore order book; the brief does not quantify its revenue contribution

quality.why: H1 FY27 revenue rose 143% to INR220.3 crore, but the brief does not split growth between organic business and the newly consolidated KIN acquisition, and H1 order inflow of about INR49 crore is weak against the INR450 crore H2 target, so the headline growth is partly acquisition-driven and its recurring rate is unclear.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets a 20-30% EBITDA margin (currently 22%) within 6 months to 1 year, but declined to commit to a 15-18% PAT margin for FY28 and holds a 10-12% PAT floor.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The main capacity addition is the already-acquired KIN Coimbatore facility (>2 lakh sq ft, INR41 crore cash), so no new plant or line is guided within the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR500 crore+ (H1 FY27 revenue INR220.3 crore, up 143%) and FY28 at INR750 crore, backed by a INR610 crore order book, but H1 order inflow was only ~INR49 crore against a INR450 crore target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says current borrowings are enough for the INR750 crore FY28 plan for at least a year and no equity raise is needed for 6-7 months; no new capex is discussed beyond the KIN acquisition.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance was only held at INR500 crore+, and management is being selective on bids with inflow of ~INR49 crore in H1 against a INR450 crore target, so an upgrade looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The INR750-800 crore closing order book depends on INR450 crore of fresh inflows versus ~INR49 crore in H1, aluminium cost pressure is forcing re-tendering, and receivables of ~INR263 crore carry 21.8% beyond 180 days.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The Big Bang Boom defence JV is to be announced in days or weeks, the Vande Bharat sleeper interior contract (INR34.85 crore incl. GST) is starting, and the KTK platform screen door MoU opens metro tenders with a INR1,500-2,000 crore a year market.

rows.label: Defence and aerospace pipeline (Big Bang Boom JV, tender orders of INR50-150 cro
rows.why: The JV is pending with no firm date and management says it is running ahead of plan, while the defence share is about 10% of FY27-28 revenue and rising in FY28, so conversion is uncertain.

rows.label: Debtor days fall and positive operating cash flow in FY28
rows.when: debtor days within ~6 months; OCF FY28
rows.why: Management guided debtor days down within about 6 months and positive operating cash flow in FY28, against receivables of ~INR263 crore with 21.8% beyond 180 days and inventory days already down 19.

rows.label: KIN metro margin uplift
rows.why: Management expects better margins from KIN's metro business, which has a INR180 crore order book and export approvals from Alstom, Hitachi and Siemens, but integration is still early.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY27 INR500 crore+ and FY28 INR750 crore revenue targets and the 20-30% EBITDA ambition, but was evasive on order timing, the Big Bang Boom JV and PAT beyond the 10-12% band; analysts pressed on the low H1 order inflow of ~INR49 crore and on receivables.
